title: Limit of the matching-run probability
statement: Let $p:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. For each $K$, choose uniformly a binary word of length $K$ and compare it with the first $K$ bits of $p$; the run returns true precisely when the first differing bit of the word is $1$, and returns no value if there is no differing bit. As $K$ tends to infinity, the probability that the run returns true converges to the real number $\sum_{i\ge 0}p_i2^{-(i+1)}$, with bits interpreted as $0$ or $1$.
